reason: The defect and the need for a place() pass are real and I reproduced them at 1440: one press of −7 puts invitations at 16 days / top 224px, the pixel menu tasting already holds (measured, both top:224), and after the press data-lead is still on menu tasting and .b-gapNote still reads "Nothing is planned for the next 16 days" — both are written once at render and never re-derived, so a re-layout hook is genuinely missing. But the MERGE step as written is wrong for this direction and trades a visible overlap for a silent lie. Three measured reasons. (1) The rule is proximity, not same-day: a collapsed .b-item measures 79px against 14px/day, so "within the previous item's measured offsetHeight" merges anything up to 5.6 days apart into one row with ONE tick and ONE count. Two −1 presses put invitations at 21 days / top 294 while menu tasting occupies 224–303; the rule fires and the count column — the column this whole direction is — tells the reader 16 when the truth is 21. That is precisely the "quietly fudging the close ones" that render-b.js's SCALE comment and lock.md's pixels-per-day clause refuse; an overlap looks broken, a merge reads as correct and is not. (2) With the editor open the merged row is 378px tall, so the walk cascades: from the same two −1 presses my simulation merges invitations (21d), final dress fitting (37d) AND choose the evening music (44d) into the 16-day row. The open editor eats the next three moments and dates them all to 16 days. (3) Merging reparents the edited .b-item into another .b-item; I probed it, and moving the subtree that holds the focused stepper drops document.activeElement to BODY, so the signature gesture dies after one keyboard press. It also breaks per-item identity that the rest of the file depends on: data-lead bolds .b-title for every title in the row, one row would carry two .b-grab buttons under one count, states["owner-editing"] finds its host by [data-id], and it violates the existing gate assertion "the stepper moves nothing but the item being edited" (interaction-check.mjs line ~305) — pulling one thing nearer must not drag another item's title into your row.
sharpenedFix: Keep place() in render-b.js, drop the proximity merge. place(measureEl) should: read each item's days-away from data-away (default its fixture value), clamp the edited value to 1..F.toDay(), sort ascending, move data-lead onto the nearest item only, re-derive the .b-gapNote text from that nearest value, and write style.top = away * data-px — mutating attributes and style only, never reparenting a node, so the focused stepper button survives (I measured focus dropping to BODY on a reparent). Handle the two overlap cases separately and honestly. SAME DAY (data-away exactly equal) is the only case that may share a mark: group those items into one .b-item at that true top with one .b-tick and one count in the gutter, each moment keeping its own title line and its own .b-grab, only the nearest of the group taking data-lead weight, and the group announced as one list entry — two things on one day is a real wedding. NEAR BUT NOT EQUAL must stay on its true pixel: leave every tick and every count at away * px and push only the text block of the later item down by the minimum overlap, so proportionality survives and the mark still points at the real day; if that de-collision is judged too fussy, the honest fallback is to leave the rows where they are and accept the tight pair, never to restate one item's date as another's. Then extend the primary-gesture block in interaction-check.mjs, repeated at 390 / 901 / 1440: after one −7 and after ten +7 clicks assert zero collisions among .b-measure .b-item, assert every item's bottom is inside .b-measure's box, assert exactly one [data-lead="true"] and that it is the nearest by count, assert .b-gapNote's number equals that nearest count, and — the one this fix most needs — assert that no item's rendered days-away ever disagrees with its own top / data-px.
